text:
maria_s: Quick question — I'm prototyping ephemeral TLS certs for edge proxies (1h lifetime) to reduce blast radius if a cert is leaked. Curious about RBAC and KMS implications across cloud + on-prem. Anyone run this at scale?

alex_infra: We experimented with short certs in a few service pools last year. Main ops items: automated rotation flow, strong audit events for each mint, and a clear fallback if KMS is unreachable. Are you planning ACME/on-cluster signing or using our KMS-as-signing-service?

tyler_security: Ephemeral certs are 👍 for security, but list of must-haves: strict RBAC so only the proxy pool SAs can call kms:Sign / kms:AsymmetricSign, per-rotation audit entries, and an emergency rotation playbook. Also, we need to ensure we can prove provenance (timestamps + signer id) for compliance.

jordan_prod: Note about perf: rotating every hour might affect TLS session resumption and connection churn for long-lived clients. Consider staggered rollouts and session ticket compatibility. For Dedicated we usually avoid <4h without testing.

maria_s: Plan is: proxies call a signing service which talks to KMS (so we don't grant KMS access to thousands of nodes). That service will mint certs and write an audit event to our audit-log topic + push a short-lived secret to the proxy. Thoughts on that design?

infra-bot: deployment notice: cert-rotator-service v0.3.1 rolled to staging at 2412345700 :rocket: (no errors)

tyler_security: That pattern is better — a narrow-privilege signing service. Make sure the signing service has mTLS to KMS and that KMS requests include key provenance metadata. RBAC for that service should be limited to specific key versions. Also: require TLS 1.3 only on the edge, enable TLS ticket encryption rotation, and disable legacy ciphers.

sanjay_devex: For KMS outage: we could cache the last-good cert or allow the signing service to issue a short extension (e.g., +15m) when KMS is flakey, but that increases risk. Alternative: have a standby key in a secondary region/HSM replica that the signing service can failover to under strict audit and alerting.

maria_s: Ok — two follow-ups: 1) exact KMS IAM bindings to request so I can open the PR; 2) suggested audit event schema for rotation (what fields to include). Anyone have a minimal example?

tyler_security: IAM bindings: principal: serviceAccount:cert-rotator@redwood. roles: kms.signAsymmetric (or equivalent), kms.getPublicKey, kms.getKeyVersion. Scope to resource: projects/*/locations/*/keyRings/edge-signing/cryptoKeys/edge-priv. For audit schema: timestamp, signer_service_id, key_version, cert_serial, subject, validity_start, validity_end, requester_ip, request_id, trace_id, region, fallback_used (bool), reason_code (if fallback).

alex_infra: Add also "rotation_trigger" (manual/schedule/auto-detect) and include any policy-id used for RBAC so we can reconcile later. Keep events small but indexed by key_version and cert_serial for quick searches.

jordan_prod: For incident playbook: if a private key compromise suspected -> 1) mark keyVersion compromised in KMS, 2) spin new keyVersion and force immediate reissue across regions, 3) update proxies with new certs via rollout (canary first), 4) publish audit summary and notify legal/compliance. Practice this in drills.

maria_s: Great — I'll draft the IAM PR and an audit JSON schema based on Tyler's list. One remaining question: do we require CT logs for these short-lived certs? We aren't using public identities for some internal customer-facing proxies.

tyler_security: For internal/internal-customer proxies we don't need public CT. But if certs are used for externally-verifiable service identity, prefer logging to CT or our internal transparency ledger. Make sure our audit events include a hash we can reconcile with any external logs.

alex_infra: Also remember OCSP stapling: even with 1h certs, stapling reduces client latency and keeps revocation fast. Configure stapling on the proxy and monitor staple freshness.

maria_s: Thanks all — I'll post the PR link here in the next 24h and add a short runbook for fallback failover. If anyone wants to pair on the KMS policy ping me :slightly_smiling_face:

sanjay_devex: I'll review the runbook. Also recommend adding a smoke check that verifies proxy certs rotate successfully every 2h in staging and alerts if rotation fails twice.

infra-bot: uptime monitor: cert-rotator-service healthchecks OK at 2412345818 :white_check_mark:
